scenes.heading: Mount Points
scenes.narration: A mount point attaches an external cloud storage location into DBFS so you can access it with a simple local-style path.

scenes.heading: Why mount storage
bullets: Access ADLS or S3 with clean paths
scenes.narration: Mounting lets you reach an ADLS or S3 container using a clean path like slash mnt slash raw. You configure the credentials a single time at mount, so notebooks do not repeat secrets. And every notebook and job then shares that same convenient location.

scenes.heading: Creating a mount
scenes.narration: This call mounts an Azure Blob container at the path slash mnt slash raw. The credential is pulled from a secret scope rather than hard-coded, which keeps keys out of the notebook. After this runs, any code can read from slash mnt slash raw directly.

scenes.text: New workspaces increasingly favor Unity Catalog external locations over mounts for centralized, auditable access control.
scenes.narration: Newer workspaces increasingly favor Unity Catalog external locations over mounts, because they give centralized and auditable access control.
